summary:
# NOTES: *Thomas Wingfold, Curate*, Vol I (of III), by George MacDonald. Chapters I–XXXIII, ends "END OF THE FIRST VOLUME."

## Cast and places
- **Helen Lingard**: 23, tall, blue eyes, dark hair, fair skin, regular features, "over-still" face. Her own mistress. Never called Nelly. Drawing-master: she'd "wake up about forty." Plays piano woodenly. Loves brother Leopold most; likes cousin George next. Dull, sensible, not yet awake.
- **Leopold "Poldie" Lingard**: Helen's brother, ~20, at Cambridge. Swarthy, dark hair, large lustrous eyes, slender. Mother was a high-caste Hindoo lady. Raised from age ~8 by father's elder brother (Goldswyre, Yorkshire estate). Addicted to a drug.
- **Father**: army officer, went to India, rose high, made fortune, died; split fortune equally between Helen and Leopold. Helen's mother died at Helen's birth.
- **Mrs. Ramshorn**: Helen's aunt, widow of the dean of Halystone. Childless, peevish, sees herself as wronged. Secretly runs the house. Wants fortune kept in family. Later wrote most of her late husband's sermons; reveals this in Ch XXIX.
- **George Bascombe**: Mrs. R's nephew, son of her younger sister and a northern canon. Law student "eating his way to the bar." Tall, handsome, "Apollo," "Hercules," Havannah cigars, bass voice, sings his own song. Self-styled prophet who destroys others' beliefs. Lays down the law. Says "I like you... I am open as the day." Thinks of Helen as a wife. Believes in no afterlife and in punishing wrongdoers.
- **Thomas Wingfold**: curate of Glaston Abbey church, 26 (text also says he looks ~30). Middle height, good forehead, "questionable nose," clear grey eyes, long sensitive mouth, large chin, pale, straight black hair. Shy, honest, never lies, does not believe clearly. Says "Don't you think?" Had an elder brother who died (Polwarth says he had "my brother, who is dead"). Uncle **Jonah Driftwood, D.D.**, left him 157 hand-written sermons. The rector is absent; the living's presentation belongs to Wingfold's family. Rector is "the last man in the world" to plagiarize, per Mrs R.
- **Joseph Polwarth**: gate-keeper at Osterfield Park, "the Park-Gate." Small, deformed, asthmatic, huge head, white hair, dry husky voice, dignified. Cornish family, lost estate through gambling. Father tall and handsome. Brothers died young except Robert (died at 50; left Rachel £20/yr). Polwarth has £30/yr of his own. Cottage rent-free. Keeps an attic study of books. Wrote Wingfold the anonymous-style letter (Ch XIV). Was bullied at school, pushed a boy into a pond, found Christ through Matthew 1:21.
- **Rachel Polwarth**: his niece, ~ small child's size, deformed, big head, rich brown hair, sweet face, thin, sensitive mouth, tiny hands and feet. Sings in a weak sweet voice. Keeps house. Wrote out a manuscript that Wingfold returns (Ch XII). Her eyes "look through sorrow to something beyond."
- **Lord de Barre**: owner of Osterfield; new earl building new house. Foundations laid 20 years earlier by uncle of present earl. Old house "Glaston" in hollow over a lake; ghost-story lady drowned in a sack; hidden room with trap and well-like cellar.
- **Emmeline** (surname unnamed): flaxen-haired, eldest daughter of a retired manufacturer near Goldswyre; manipulative; engaged to **Captain Hodges** (dragoon). Killed by Leopold.
- **Mr. Faber**: new doctor, cold, unbelieving, business-like. **Mr. Bird**: old doctor, dead, "a gossip." **Mr. Drew**: linendraper. **Jones**: groom. **Fanny**: Helen's good horse; Helen rides an "old cocktail" horse.
- **Places**: Glaston (old town), Abbey church, river Lythe, Osterfield Park, Mrs R's red-brick Queen Anne house with ancient garden and sunk fence, Millpool road, Goldswyre (Yorkshire), Cambridge, Eton, Trinity.

## Chronology of events

**Ch I (Helen Lingard).** November Friday. Wind roars in chimneys. Helen has not gone out; wrote a long letter to Leopold; reads a novel where heroine marries an unworthy man. Feels bored; nearly thinks, then falls asleep. Background on her family as above. Expects Bascombe and curate to dine.

**Ch II (Wingfold).** Morning walk by river to a stone. Thinks of his life: Oxford, ordination, "servant who abideth not in the house for ever." Recites Horace (Inachus, Orcus, urn, "boat of eternal exile"). Feels no fire.

**Ch III (Diners).** Mrs R describes Helen's property, George's coming visit, Wingfold's position. Wingfold is curate of the "miserable living" and rector non-resident. Descriptions of Wingfold and George. Dinner. Mrs R in black velvet with Venetian lace; Helen in black silk with Honiton.

**Ch IV (Talk).** At dinner: book of poems Helen received; George mocks it. Trinity fellow's verse "Heard'st thou a quiver and clang? ... But the lyre-shell was my heart." Horace talk: acorn-cup; "illusions." George's song "Each man has his lampful of oil," "Sunshine and Wind," "For the day draws nigh when we all go out!" Helen: "heathenish." Wingfold: Horace is "sad." Piano recital; Wingfold thinks Helen's face "had no story."

**Ch V (Staggering Question).** Moonlight walk with George to gate. George looks back at church tower and asks, "do you believe one word of all that?" Accuses the church of imitation and Christians of fear of death. Calls Wingfold "humbug," says he eats bread from church "as somebody says in your own blessed Bible." Wingfold: "I decline to place myself between the horns of any such dilemma." Parted without handshake.

**Ch VI (Churchyard).** Wingfold sits on gravestone; feels humiliated and questions everything. Considers Paley, Butler, Leighton, Neander, Coleridge, Liddon. Sunday approaches; many books, little time.

**Ch VII (Cousins).** George's creed: destroy beliefs; no capacity for the unknown. Helen's education and dormant soul described. Garden description. Helen trims chrysanthemums on balcony; runs down to George.

**Ch VIII (Garden).** Cigar talk. "I like it diluted." George: "born-fools," "mutual compassion," the wife-beater, "die her enemy and friend of Death." Helen admires him. George considers marrying her ("cauliflower of the spine," natural selection).

**Ch IX (Park).** Walk through sunk-fence door to park. Birds in winter; nature "rather a good-natured old woman." New house and old house in hollow. Helen and Poldie explored it as children; trap door over pit. George: "If it had but a brain and a tongue it could tell tales." Helen dislikes the hole.

**Ch X (Dwarfs).** They meet a deformed woman (<4 ft, crab walk) and her asthmatic uncle. George: "ought to have been strangled"; wants laws against deformed marriage. Helen: "Unfortunately they have all got mothers." George's law/punishment lecture. Sunday: Abbey service; Mrs R's view on forgiveness vs. forgetting. George leaves; Helen's brother's background; Leopold's Cambridge trouble rumour.

**Ch XI (Curate at Home).** Wingfold restless, "born again" hinted. Reads uncle's sermons; none fit. Prays and loses faith ("driver to that chariot"). Rushes out to fields.

**Ch XII (Incident).** All Hallows' summer morning. Finds manuscript volume dropped by Rachel on path; returns it: "Do not be alarmed: I have not read one word of it." Her reply: "I see I need not have been afraid." Weeks of darkness; child smiles at him; hawthorn bud.

**Ch XIII (Report of Progress).** George courts Helen with "MAKING." Helen accepts his doctrines. Narrator comments on life/death. George: "truth is truth"; narrator rebuts with "you cannot be convinced there is no God." No formal offer yet.

**Ch XIV (Jeremy Taylor).** Spring Tuesday. Letter from Joseph Polwarth, The Park-Gate: uncle's sermon wholly Jeremy Taylor's; Wingfold sat in free seat; Polwarth not wanting to humiliate him. Wingfold stunned; reflects on plagiarism.

**Ch XV (Park Gate).** Wingfold replies; walks to Park Gate; Rachel answers door. "Come in, sir, please." Polwarth absent (steward called him to new house). Description of cottage, Rachel's face.

**Ch XVI (Attic).** Polwarth's book-filled attic. Wingfold confesses the sermon and his uncle Jonah Driftwood's legacy. Polwarth: preach what feeds you; "if he feed not the flock... hireling." "How straight an honest bow can shoot!" (Wingfold's thought).

**Ch XVII (Polwarth's Plan).** "Second-hand goods." Polwarth on Moses and deformity. Wingfold: "I cannot even prove there is a God." Polwarth: "I know him in my heart... As well ask a fly..." Question: "Was Jesus true?" Wingfold can't say what Christ was.

**Ch XVIII (Joseph Polwarth).** Polwarth tells his life: family history, schooling, bullying, pond incident, hidden garret den, prayer, Matthew 1:21, "I had seen the man Christ Jesus, and in him had known the Father."

**Ch XIX (Conclusion).** Polwarth: church exists to assert Jesus is the Son and revealer of the Father; "Take your New Testament... read--to find out." Wingfold resolves to keep curacy a month, then resign if no prospect. Thanks Bascombe grudgingly.

**Ch XX (Strange Sermon).** Sunday. Text "Confessing your faults one to another." Wingfold confesses using others' sermons; "gleaning in other men's fields" (Polwarth's extracts). Congregation split. Mrs R indignant. Bascombe now praises his "pluck"; Helen liked it. Mrs R: "The rector!... STEALS from them." Bascombe thinks of the sermon's simile as absurd.

**Ch XXI (Thunderbolt).** One night Helen sews a cap for aunt's birthday. Tap at window: Leopold, face like a spectre, bloody wristband. "Helen, I am a murderer... They will be here before daylight." Asks to be hidden. "Come in, Poldie, and tell me all about it." Helen swears "So help me God, I will not!"

**Ch XXII (Leopold).** Locks door; drinks brandy. Helen fetches bread and wine. Leopold confesses "She" (girl) is dead; mentions a shaft and a girl in a wood. They leave by window to the garden, park door, meadows. Helen wears dark shawl.

**Ch XXIII (Refuge).** Dark walk to deserted house. Leopold hates the hidden room: "I knew it at the time." Helen sings him a lullaby. Whistling signal arranged. Leopold has a knife in breast pocket and a silver box of the drug.

**Ch XXIV (Secret).** Dawn; Helen runs back, faints. Cap finished; aunt's birthday. Helen hides her fear; discovers her gift for concealment.

**Ch XXV (Daylight Visit).** Helen walks to Park Gate; passes Rachel singing and says "Good day, Rachel." Helen prays for first time ("I am his sister, thou knowest!"). Macbeth: "To know my deed, 'twere best not know myself." Returns to Leopold; he has the knife; she takes the bloodied shirt to destroy. Gives him water from garden well, food.

**Ch XXVI (Leopold's Story, I).** Emmeline, eldest of manufacturer's family near Goldswyre. Her "black ewe" schoolmate; school produces shallow mothers. Leopold, after Eton and a year's reading with a cousin's tutor, fell in love with her at a ball. She toys with his jealousy. He falls into drug experiments at Cambridge.

**Ch XXVII (Leopold's Story, II).** Ball given by Emmeline's family; fancy dress and masks. Leopold in cloak, felt hat, black silk mask. Drug dose on journey. Note "Meet me for one long minute at the circle." Emmeline in Diana costume; accepts note. Drug-induced visions. He sees her waltz with Captain Hodges. Hallucination-filled vision; she says "I am going to be married to Captain Hodges" and kisses him. He stabs her with skean-dhu (Highland knife, sharp, needle-pointed) and she dies. He nearly throws himself down a coalpit shaft; throws in cloak and mask; flees to Helen. Newspapers: "mysterious murder of a young lady in Yorkshire," a week elapsed.

**Ch XXVIII (Sisterhood).** Helen: "I would rather be you than she!" Helen takes knife (Leopold's name engraved on silver handle). Helen's love and protective passion. Aunt Mrs R's account of husband's sermons (she wrote them). Mr Faber called in.

**Ch XXIX (Sick-Chamber).** Leopold's cry in night; Helen finds him rigid on bed; takes him to her room. Brain fever. Helen tells aunt; aunt approves; servants sworn to silence. Mr Faber attends; weeks of fever. Helen's life now "a thing of worth." Helen goes to church.

**Ch XXX (Curate's Progress).** Wingfold studies NT with Polwarth: genealogy discrepancies; "primarily" (what Jesus came to do); miracles; "Was Jesus true?" Polwarth prays for Wingfold walking round the house at night.

**Ch XXXI (Discovery).** Wingfold reads a harmony; "Why call ye me Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?" (Luke 6:46). Then "IF ANY MAN WILL DO HIS WILL..." (John 7:17). Visits an old woman. Next Sunday: sermon: "I call not myself a Christian." Vows to obey Jesus. Reactions: Mrs R "Socinian"/"infidel"; churchwarden (ex-Wesleyan) "There's stuff in the fellow!"; Bascombe: "he'd make a fellow fancy he did believe..." Helen listens; Polwarth weeps with gladness.

**Ch XXXII (Hopes).** Helen attends church (first time since Leopold). Leopold asks why church; asks for George. Helen refuses to bring George to the sick-room. Helen comes to believe Leopold innocent (may be drug-hallucination). Leopold: "If you forget me, an enemy will think of me." Plans ride with George Saturday evening.

**Ch XXXIII (Ride).** Sunset ride on Helen's old horse; cousin's talk of mortality and of ceasing to be; Helen weeps and gallops away. Near the deserted house. George speaks of murder: a coastguardsman saw a third man jump into a boat; no trace; suspicion of "some squire of low degree"; George "strongly inclined" to investigate. Helen dissembles. George: "Every murderer hanged, or better, imprisoned for life, is a gain to the community." Helen returns home. End of Vol I.
